messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Sex: Male
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital Course:

The patient, an 18-year-old male with no significant past medical history, was admitted to the emergency department with complaints of suprapubic and periumbilical pain, accompanied by nausea for one day. Physical examination revealed mild tenderness to palpation in the periumbilical, right lower quadrant, and left upper quadrant regions. Respiratory rate, heart rate, and blood pressure were within normal limits, but complete blood count revealed leukocytosis with a left shift.

A CT exam was performed to rule out any underlying causes of the aforementioned symptoms, demonstrating a dilated and hyperenhancing retrocecal appendix containing a form of calcified materials within it. Moreover, small air collections were identified anterior to the right and left common iliac arteries, and posterior to both psoas muscles in the retroperitoneal cavity of the abdomen.

The patient was taken to the operating room for an appendectomy, during which an additional inflamed appendix, and evidence of minor perforation into the retroperitoneum were found. Surgical team continued with appendectomy in view of inferior incision area revealing no pathologic process in the retroperitoneal cavity.

The patient was monitored in the post-operative care unit and demonstrated no post-operative complications. The patient was discharged the following day in stable condition.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Instructions:

The patient is advised to take all prescribed medications and attend follow-up appointments as scheduled. Discharge instructions and the post-operative care plan have been explained to the patient in detail before being discharged.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Acute appendicitis with a faecolith, perforated into the retroperitoneum and treated by appendectomy, is chiefly responsible for the admission. It belongs to ICD-10-AM chapter K, diseases of the digestive system. The category is K35, acute appendicitis.

CODE: K35
